selection.rule: Dependency-complete first 24 questions from the question-sheet selection order.

questions.question: What teaching from the Qur’an is mentioned near the beginning of the passage about the prayers?
questions.answer: It says that the prayers are required for believers at set times.

questions.question: What complaint did the older man make about praying?
questions.answer: He said praying five times every day felt too much and became tiring because it keeps repeating.

questions.question: When the speaker later listened to his own inner self, what did he notice?
questions.answer: He noticed that his own nafs was saying the same complaint.

questions.question: What reason is given for why the nafs spoke that way?
questions.answer: It was listening through laziness and taking that idea from Satan.

questions.question: What did the speaker understand about those words after hearing them again in himself?
questions.answer: He understood that they represented the voice of the evil-commanding soul and were influenced by whisperings.

questions.question: Why did the speaker decide to start with himself instead of others?
questions.answer: He realized that a person who has not corrected his own nafs cannot properly guide other people.

questions.question: How does the speaker describe the state in which the nafs said those words?
questions.answer: He describes it as ignorance mixed together, laziness, and heedlessness.

questions.question: What was the speaker planning to give his nafs in response?
questions.answer: He was going to give it five warnings.

questions.question: Who is being addressed directly in most of this passage?
questions.answer: The speaker’s own nafs, or lower self.

questions.question: What kind of person first spoke the complaint about prayer?
questions.answer: He was someone advanced in age, strong in body, and high in status.

questions.question: What positive thing did that man still say about the prayers before complaining?
questions.answer: He admitted that the prayers are good.

questions.question: What was his main problem with them?
questions.answer: He thought doing them every day five times was excessive and exhausting.

questions.question: How much time passed before the speaker reflected on that complaint in himself?
questions.answer: A long time passed.

questions.question: What does the phrase about the “ear of laziness” show about the nafs?
questions.answer: It shows that laziness makes the nafs ready to accept bad suggestions.

questions.question: According to the passage, what source was feeding the nafs this complaint?
questions.answer: Satan was feeding it that complaint.

questions.question: What does the speaker’s response teach about self-improvement?
questions.answer: It teaches that a person should first work on fixing his own inner faults before trying to fix others.

questions.question: What is the main issue being discussed in this passage?
questions.answer: The passage discusses why some people feel burdened by praying five times daily and how that objection should be answered.

questions.question: How is the older man’s objection described in simple terms?
questions.answer: He felt the prayers were good in themselves, but too frequent to keep doing every day.

questions.question: What happened when the speaker examined his own inner self?
questions.answer: He found the same objection inside himself.

questions.question: What does this discovery suggest about the problem?
questions.answer: It suggests that this is not just one person’s problem but a common struggle of the human nafs.

questions.question: What connection does the passage make between laziness and Satan?
questions.answer: It shows that laziness opens a person up to Satan’s whispering.

questions.question: Why does the speaker say he must begin with his own nafs?
questions.answer: Because personal reform has to come before guiding others.

questions.question: What kind of condition was the nafs in when it made those excuses?
questions.answer: It was in a state of idleness, heedlessness, and deep ignorance.

questions.question: What structure does the speaker announce at the end of the passage?
questions.answer: He announces that he will answer with five warnings.
